title: Brain – one window for all your Claude Code sessions

scenes.say: If you run a lot of Claude Code sessions at the same time, you know the feeling. A dozen terminal windows, and somewhere in there, one session has been waiting for you for ten minutes. Brain is a small native Mac app that keeps an eye on all of them for you.
This is Brain. On the left is every running session, across all of your Claude accounts. On the right is the one you have selected.

At the top are the sessions that need you. Red means Claude has a question, or is waiting for a permission. Amber means a session finished its turn, and it's your move. The longest wait is always on top, and the number tells you how long it has been waiting.
Here, the API gateway session asks whether its rate limits should apply per tenant, or globally. Claude wrote that question itself. More on how in a moment.
Below are the sessions that are still working, each with a short line about what it is doing right now. And further down, the ones that have been resting for a while.

On the right, you read the latest messages of the selected session. Your prompts, Claude's replies, nicely formatted, and every tool call as a single line. So you know what happened, without switching to the terminal.
The timeline shows every event of the session, in order. Prompts, permission requests, finished turns, and the status reports Claude sent along the way.
When you're ready to answer, press Return. Brain brings the right iTerm window, tab and split pane to the front, and you're right where Claude is waiting.
If you work with more than one Claude account, Brain finds all of them on its own. Press Tab to filter by account.
Press slash to search. Brain matches the session name, the project path, the account and the last message.
And press R to give a session a better name. Brain sends Claude Code's own rename command, so the new name shows up in your terminal as well.

So how does Brain know all this? From two sources. Claude Code hooks report automatically, when you send a prompt, when a permission is needed, and when a turn ends. And a short section in your CLAUDE dot M D asks Claude to report what it is doing, and what it is waiting for, with a single command: brain report.
Whenever a session starts waiting for you, Brain also sends a notification. So you can stay focused on something else, and still never keep Claude waiting.
Getting started takes one script. It builds the app, installs the brain command, and adds the hooks to every Claude account, with a backup of every file it touches.
Brain is open source. You'll find it on GitHub, at martin emmert, slash, big brain claude. Thanks for watching.
